props.gloss_en: the mishnah: where the custom is to bless [over the Megillah], one blesses; where it is not, one does not
Abaye: they taught [the custom clause] only of the blessing after it
but before it, it is a mitzva to bless
as Rav Yehuda said in Shmuel's name: for all the mitzvot one blesses over them עובר their performance
the word 'over' [in Shmuel's dictum] is the language of preceding -- the reading the stam's question asks a source for
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: the verse says 'and Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain and passed (ויעבר) the Cushite' (II Samuel 18:23)
Abaye: from here -- 'and he passed (עבר) before them' (Genesis 33:3)
and if you wish, say from here: 'and their king passed (ויעבר) before them, and the Lord at their head' (Micah 2:13)
what does one bless before it? Rav Sheshet of Katrazya came before Rav Ashi and blessed מנ״ח
what does one bless after it? Blessed are You... who pleads our cause, judges our claim, avenges our vengeance, punishes our foes for us, and pays recompense to all the enemies of our soul
[its closing:] Blessed are You, Lord, who exacts payment for Israel from all their foes
Rav Pappa: therefore let us say both: Blessed are You, Lord, who exacts payment for Israel from all their foes, the God who saves

הלכך נימרינהו לתרוייהו -- the first closing, הנפרע לישראל מכל צריהם, is one of the two combined
הלכך נימרינהו לתרוייהו -- Rava's האל המושיע is the other
